metadata.title: On the Choice of the Item Response Model for Scaling PISA Data: Model Selection Based on Information Criteria and Quantifying Model Uncertainty

design_fields.q1_rationale: The study used multiple plausible values and applied Rubin's rules for handling them.
design_fields.q2_rationale: The study explicitly states that student weights were used in the analysis.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study does not mention using multilevel modeling or any method that accounts for school clustering in the analysis.
design_fields.q4_rationale: There is no mention of any validation strategy beyond the estimation sample in the provided excerpts.
design_fields._pdf_matched: 154. Robitzsch (2022). On the Choice of the Item Response Model for Scaling PISA Data: Model Selection Based on Information Criteria and Quantifying Model Uncertainty.pdf
design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): The study compares 11 unidimensional IRT scaling models for PISA 2009 mathematics/reading/science and quantifies model uncertainty (ME, MEbc, ER, TE) for country means/SD/percentiles; no separate per-country/system analysis across countries is described.
